finding: Every 'overall' figure conceals a large per-dimension spread. sov34's 45.26% spans 93.94 (retrieval faithfulness) to 15.65 (regional law) — 78 points. The models are strong at NOT BEING FOOLED and weak at GOVERNANCE SUBSTANCE, which is the inverse of what a governance product claims.

RETRACTION_2026-08-04.status: THE CONCLUSION IN THIS FILE IS RETRACTED — the low scores are largely a GRADER ARTIFACT
RETRACTION_2026-08-04.defect: grade_response scores `expect_contains` as matches/len(list) — i.e. it treats the keyword list as a CONJUNCTION (all required). In 138 of 146 items (95%) the list holds 3-9 keywords that are plainly ALTERNATIVES, not requirements.
RETRACTION_2026-08-04.proof: sov34 asked 'Name a jurisdiction whose AI governance approach is voluntary/advisory' answered 'Singapore ... voluntary ... framework' — a CORRECT answer — and scored 0.375, because it did not also say japan, uk, verify and 'model ai governance'. It cannot name one jurisdiction and also name four others.
RETRACTION_2026-08-04.implication: 'Weak at governance substance' is NOT established. The dimensions I called collapsed are the ones with the longest keyword lists — regional_law 6/6 items, compliance 10/10, accountability 11/11, ethics 11/11, sigil_chain 8/8. The measured floor is the grader's ceiling, not the models'.
RETRACTION_2026-08-04.what_survives: The per-dimension SPREAD finding survives — an overall figure still conceals a 73-100pp range, and that is why per-dimension rows matter. What does not survive is the interpretation of WHICH dimensions are weak, and the product-critical mean.
RETRACTION_2026-08-04.correct_fix: Decide per item whether the list is a conjunction or alternatives, and grade accordingly. Do NOT globally switch to any-match: that would over-credit items where several keywords genuinely are required. This needs an item-level audit of all 146.

RETRACTION_VALIDATED_2026-08-04.question: Was the retraction of 'models are weak at governance substance' correct?
RETRACTION_VALIDATED_2026-08-04.test: Re-scored the same models on the same 193 items with expect_mode active (63 any / 83 all).

RETRACTION_VALIDATED_2026-08-04.verdict: RETRACTION CONFIRMED CORRECT. Correcting answer-set semantics moved one model +13.12 points on identical items. The published board understated the fleet by roughly that margin wherever long keyword lists dominated a dimension.
RETRACTION_VALIDATED_2026-08-04.caveat: One model, one re-run. sov34 timed out so the comparison is n=1. The direction and rough magnitude are established; the per-dimension detail is not, and the +13.12 should not be quoted as a fleet-wide correction until more arms are re-measured.
RETRACTION_VALIDATED_2026-08-04.consequence: Every GovBench figure published before this fix — including the 45.26/41.70/38.35/35.40/32.71 board and the per-dimension spread analysis — was measured on an instrument with a known floor. They are superseded, not merely caveated.
